bibleSpine.kjv: But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ's very conception is of the Holy Ghost — He begins human life already inside the Spirit-filled, God-surrendered existence.

bibleSpine.kjv: And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
bibleSpine.gloss: The source-term: 'that holy thing... shall be called the Son of God.' Holy Ghost + power of the Highest = the pattern of both His birth and ours (Acts 1:8).

bibleSpine.kjv: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
bibleSpine.gloss: From childhood the Father's will was already His life — the surrendered life did not begin at Jordan; it was His from the first.

bibleSpine.kjv: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.
bibleSpine.gloss: Messianic — the law WITHIN the heart, not merely obeyed from without. The delight-to-obey that the new birth reproduces in us (Ezek. 36:26-27).

bibleSpine.kjv: Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.
bibleSpine.gloss: Source-term: 'The Son can do nothing of himself.' Christ disclaims independent power — He lived by dependence, as man must.

bibleSpine.kjv: I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.
bibleSpine.gloss: The same confession restated — not His own will but the Father's. The surrendered will is the mechanism of the sinless life.

bibleSpine.kjv: Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the words that I speak unto you I speak not of myself: but the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works.
bibleSpine.gloss: Source-term: 'the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works.' The works were the Father's through an indwelt, surrendered man — the very arrangement offered to us.

bibleSpine.kjv: As the living Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father: so he that eateth me, even he shall live by me.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ names the pattern and hands it over: 'I live by the Father: so... he shall live by me.' The dependence He lived by becomes the dependence we live by.

bibleSpine.kjv: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother's womb, and be born? Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.
bibleSpine.gloss: Source-term: 'except a man be born of water and of the Spirit.' The new-birth charter — the whole man re-created; what Christ was from His birth we become by ours.

bibleSpine.kjv: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;
bibleSpine.gloss: Source-term: 'the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost' — the laver-truth: cleansing (washing) joined to power (renewing of the Spirit), not by works.

bibleSpine.kjv: That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word,
bibleSpine.gloss: Source-term: 'the washing of water by the word.' The laver's water is the word — cleansing is done by water AND word AND Spirit together (Titus 3:5; John 3:5).

bibleSpine.kjv: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.
bibleSpine.gloss: The OT laver-and-new-birth prophecy: clean water (washing) + new heart + My Spirit put within = cleansing joined to power, the obedience Christ had from birth (Ps. 40:8) now given to us.

bibleSpine.kjv: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.
bibleSpine.gloss: The power-source named: 'not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.' The same Spirit-not-flesh principle by which Christ lived and by which we are re-created.

bibleSpine.kjv: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
bibleSpine.gloss: The Highest-overshadowing of Luke 1:35 offered to the disciple: Holy Ghost come upon you = power. Christ's birth-endowment becomes the church's new-birth endowment.

bibleSpine.kjv: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
bibleSpine.gloss: Source-term: 'if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature.' The result of the new birth — a wholly re-made man, Christlike from the same source Christ lived from.

bibleSpine.kjv: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
bibleSpine.gloss: Source-term: 'partakers of the divine nature.' What Christ was — a partaker of the divine nature in human flesh (1SM 226.2) — the believer becomes by the new birth.

symbolDefs.symbol: the new birth (born again / born of water and of the Spirit)
symbolDefs.meaning: The Spirit re-creating the whole man — an entire change of the entire man, a new heart and new spirit given, so that the natural, inherited and cultivated tendencies are made new and the man becomes a 'new creature' able to see and enter the kingdom. It is the second, spiritual birth that puts a man where Christ stood from His first birth: inside the Spirit-filled, God-surrendered life.
receipts: John 3:3-7 — except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom; that which is born of the Spirit is spirit
2 Corinthians 5:17 — if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature; old things are passed away; all things are become new
Ezekiel 36:26-27 — a new heart will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you... and I will put my spirit within you
Titus 3:5 — the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost
2 Peter 1:4 — partakers of the divine nature

symbolDefs.symbol: the laver / the washing (regeneration by water, word, and Spirit)
symbolDefs.meaning: The cleansing of regeneration in which washing and power are joined and inseparable — the water sprinkled clean, the word that sanctifies, and the renewing of the Holy Ghost are one act. Not cleansing by human might or works but by the Spirit; the laver removes filthiness AND supplies the indwelling Spirit that causes the cleansed one to walk in God's statutes.
receipts: Titus 3:5 — saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost
Ephesians 5:26 — sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word
Ezekiel 36:25-27 — sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean... and I will put my spirit within you
Zechariah 4:6 — not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: He assumed the liabilities of human nature, to be proved and tried. In His humanity He was a partaker of the divine nature. In His incarnation He gained in a new sense the title of the Son of God. Said the angel to Mary, 'The power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God' (Luke 1:35).
witnesses.gloss: Confirms Luke 1:35 and 2 Pet. 1:4 read together: Christ in His humanity was HIMSELF 'a partaker of the divine nature' — the same phrase offered to us — 'that holy thing' being the Son of God allied by birth to the human race.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: 'The Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He seeth the Father do.'... But the Son of God was surrendered to the Father's will, and dependent upon His power. So utterly was Christ emptied of self that He made no plans for Himself. He accepted God's plans for Him... So should we depend upon God, that our lives may be the simple outworking of His will.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms John 5:19: Christ's 'can do nothing of Himself' means a life surrendered to the Father's will and dependent on His power — and closes with 'so should we depend upon God,' making His pattern ours.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: The Saviour has said of Himself, 'The Son can do nothing of Himself;' 'the Father that dwelleth in Me, He doeth the works.' John 5:19; 14:10. Then if Christ is dwelling in our hearts, He will work in us 'both to will and to do of His good pleasure.'... We shall work as He worked; we shall manifest the same spirit.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms John 5:19 and 14:10 as one truth and hands it directly to the believer: the indwelt, Father-worked life of Christ is reproduced in us — 'we shall work as He worked.'

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: If we have in any sense a more trying conflict than had Christ, then He would not be able to succor us. But our Saviour took humanity, with all its liabilities. He took the nature of man, with the possibility of yielding to temptation. We have nothing to bear which He has not endured.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the section's spine — He overcame by no power unavailable to us: He took humanity 'with all its liabilities,' so the victory He won is a victory man can win by the same means.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: In Christ the cry of humanity reached the Father of infinite pity. As a man He supplicated the throne of God till His humanity was charged with a heavenly current that should connect humanity with divinity. Receiving life from God, He imparted life to men.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms John 6:57 and 14:10: 'as a man' Christ drew from God — humanity charged with divine power through dependence, the very channel the new birth opens for us.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: 'Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.' Nicodemus knew that Christ here referred to water baptism and the renewing of the heart by the Spirit of God.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms John 3:5 as the laver-truth: 'born of water and of the Spirit' = water baptism JOINED to the renewing of the heart by the Spirit — cleansing and power together.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: All true reformation begins with soul-cleansing. It is by the washing of regeneration and the renewing of the mind through the power of the Holy Spirit, that a change is wrought in the life.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms Titus 3:5: the washing of regeneration is inseparable from the renewing power of the Holy Spirit — the laver joins cleansing to power.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Transformation of heart means an entire change of the entire man. 'Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God,' Christ declared (John 3:3). This change of heart is unseen; for it is an inward work, and yet, it is seen, because it works outward from within.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the new-birth symbol as 'an entire change of the entire man' — the Spirit re-creating the whole person, matching 2 Cor. 5:17's 'new creature.'

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: As the plant receives the sunshine, the dew, and the rain, we are to open our hearts to the Holy Spirit. The work is to be done 'not by might, nor by power, but by My Spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.' Zechariah 4:6.
witnesses.gloss: Confirms Zech. 4:6 as the law of Christian growth after the new birth: the re-created life grows by receiving the Spirit, not by human might or power.

witnesses.author: A. T. Jones
witnesses.quote: 'God sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for [on account of] sin, condemned sin in the flesh: that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.' Romans 8:3, 4. And 'He is our peace,... having abolished in His flesh the enmity,... for to make in Himself of twain [God and man] one new man, so making peace.' Ephesians 2:14, 15.
witnesses.gloss: Jones (Consecrated Way) confirms the purpose of the incarnation: Christ came in our flesh so 'the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us' who walk after the Spirit — and to make 'one new man,' the new creature of 2 Cor. 5:17.

witnesses.author: E. J. Waggoner
witnesses.quote: Sinless, yet not only counted as a sinner but actually taking upon Himself sinful nature. He was made to be sin in order that we might be made righteousness... 'For we have not a High Priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.'
witnesses.gloss: Waggoner (Christ and His Righteousness) confirms the honest two-sided truth: Christ took our fallen ('sinful') nature and was tempted in all points as we are, YET without sin — that we might be made righteousness. His nature was ours; His sinlessness was in never consenting.

witnesses.author: William Miller
witnesses.quote: That the first [advent] took place in the days of Herod, when He was conceived of the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary, went about doing good, suffered on the cross, the just for the unjust, died, was buried, arose again the third day...
witnesses.gloss: Miller confirms Matt. 1:20 / Luke 1:35 as a settled first-advent fact: the Saviour 'conceived of the Holy Ghost' — the starting point of the Spirit-filled life this section traces.

historyAnchor: The pioneer articulation belongs to the 1888-era message: Waggoner's Christ and His Righteousness (1890) and Jones's The Consecrated Way to Christian Perfection (1905) set out Christ's assumption of fallen human nature and victory by faith, which Ellen White's The Desire of Ages (1898) confirms.
uncertainties: On Christ's human nature the witnesses are quoted honestly on both sides and resolved as the pioneers did: CHR 27.3 (Waggoner) and DA 117.2 affirm He took fallen humanity's nature — weakened, tempted, 'with the possibility of yielding' — while statements guarding His sinlessness ('yet without sin', 'not only counted... but actually taking upon Himself sinful nature... in order that we might be made righteousness') are about His never consenting to sin, not about an unfallen nature. Neither side is suppressed.

Heb. 5:8-9 (learned obedience, made perfect) and Gal. 2:20 ('I live by the faith of the Son of God') were verified and are available as spine reinforcement for the 'lived by faith / we live by His faith' link, but were held back from the 16-verse spine to keep it focused; add them if the section wants the by-faith mechanism made explicit.

No local Waggoner/Jones paragraph was found that states in one sentence 'the same faith and power by which Christ lived is offered to us'; that claim rests on the Scripture spine (John 6:57; Acts 1:8; 2 Pet. 1:4) plus SC 75.2 and DA 363.1, which carry it plainly. The pioneer books confirm the incarnation/nature side; EGW carries the 'His pattern is ours' side.
